clue.text: Project further atrocity about North

indicators.note: about means placed around, so the atrocity word surrounds the compass point

parts.note: an atrocity is an outrage

explanation.surface: An atrocity is reported from somewhere up north, extending a project.
explanation.definitionFit: To outrange something is to have a greater reach than it, to project further.

clue.text: Bad times for holidays?

explanation.definitionFit: An unlucky spell is a series of poor days; read the other way, they are days off work.

clue.text: Object about odd Frenchman's tedious playing

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the object word goes round the other pieces

parts.note: a thing is an object
rum means odd or strange
M is short for monsieur, a French man

explanation.surface: A complaint about a strange Frenchman's monotonous performance.
explanation.definitionFit: Strumming monotonously on a guitar is dull repetitive playing.

clue.text: In anticipation of Con

definitions.meaning: as in saving for a rainy day, preparing for
opposed, as in pros and cons

explanation.definitionFit: One saves for a rainy day; a con is an argument opposing something.

clue.text: Deny advantage won, for example

parts.note: a gain is an advantage won
say means for example

explanation.surface: Someone disputes that a lead was won, as an illustration.
explanation.definitionFit: To gainsay is to contradict or dispute.

clue.text: What ruddy cheek of Viola!

parts.note: looks like outrage at someone's impudence, but recalls Viola's speech in Twelfth Night about a girl whose concealed love fed on her rose-pink cheek

explanation.surface: An exclamation at a woman's impertinence.
explanation.walkthrough: In Shakespeare's Twelfth Night, Viola describes a girl who let concealment 'feed on her damask cheek'; 'cheek' reads as impudence but is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: Damask is a deep pink rose colour, the shade Shakespeare gives the blushing cheek.

clue.text: Spread it a different way and it is different

indicators.note: arranged a different way means the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Rearrange the spread and it changes.
explanation.definitionFit: Disparate means essentially unlike, distinct in kind.

clue.text: Eat in a place where one could be in straits

definitions.text: place where one could be in straits

parts.note: to mess is to eat together, as in a military mess

explanation.surface: Dining at a spot where you might end up in difficulty.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sicilian city lies on the narrow sea channel between Sicily and mainland Italy.

clue.text: Season with heart of wheat, making gin

parts.note: spring is a season

indicators.note: heart of picks out the central letter of the grain word

explanation.surface: Flavouring the core of a grain to distil spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: A gin is also a snare or trap, and a springe is a noose trap for small game.

clue.text: In quest of love in service groups

parts.note: for means seeking, as in 'searching for'

indicators.note: in tells us the love letter goes inside the church service word

parts.note: matins is the morning church service
O is love, a nil score in tennis

explanation.surface: Someone searching for romance within the armed forces.
explanation.definitionFit: Formations are arrangements of troops or aircraft, organised groups.

clue.text: Severe — or tender ?

explanation.definitionFit: A sore trial is a severe one; a sore spot is tender and aching.

clue.text: Government by application

definitions.meaning: the giving of a medicine or remedy

explanation.definitionFit: The ruling executive is the administration; the dosing of a drug is also its administration.

clue.text: Secretive embracing isn't, commonly, very good

indicators.note: embracing means holding inside, so the secretive word wraps around the slang form

parts.note: sly means secretive or furtive
ain't is the common, non-standard form of isn't

explanation.surface: A remark that someone furtive and unaffectionate isn't, in plain speech, a decent person.
explanation.definitionFit: Saintly describes conduct of the highest virtue, extremely good like a holy person.

clue.text: Success at the polls is naturally a disaster

definitions.meaning: a natural disaster where earth slips downhill

explanation.definitionFit: A huge electoral victory, and also a collapse of hillside soil.

clue.text: Means of stopping OAPs getting hurt

parts.note: a dam is a barrier that stops water
old age pensioners are the aged

explanation.surface: How to stop pensioners being injured.
explanation.walkthrough: OAP is British shorthand for an old age pensioner.
explanation.definitionFit: Damaged as an adjective means harmed or injured.

clue.text: Left, eating an, odd meat dish

indicators.note: odd implies the letters are jumbled into a strange order

explanation.surface: Having gone, after consuming a strange meal of meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eating' looks like a container but is fodder: 'odd' rearranges L plus EATING AN.
explanation.definitionFit: A galantine is boned meat or poultry pressed and served cold in aspic.

clue.text: Getting behind the protection of the tanks

definitions.meaning: insulating jacket wrapped round hot-water tanks

explanation.definitionFit: Trailing others is falling back; the insulating cover on boilers and pipes is also called this.

clue.text: Light, reticent type in Civil Defence

indicators.note: in places the reticent type inside the defence abbreviation

parts.note: ARP, Air Raid Precautions, was Britain's wartime civil defence
a clam is someone who clams up, reticent

explanation.surface: A quiet member of the civil defence wardens.
explanation.walkthrough: ARP (Air Raid Precautions) was Britain's Second World War civil defence service.
explanation.definitionFit: An arc lamp is an electric light from an arc between electrodes.

clue.text: Cab, a disagreeable one

explanation.definitionFit: Victorian slang for a four-wheeled hackney carriage, and also an ill-tempered snarling person.

clue.text: Hounds, born to get birds

parts.note: eagles are birds of prey

explanation.surface: Hunting dogs bred to catch birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Beagles are small hunting dogs, a breed of hound.

clue.text: Nude gets a look in the Empire State

parts.note: in the buff means naked
lo means look

explanation.surface: A naked man takes a peek at the New York skyscraper.
explanation.walkthrough: The Empire State is the nickname of New York State, not just the building.
explanation.definitionFit: Buffalo is a city in New York State, nicknamed the Empire State.

clue.text: Still stuffy

explanation.definitionFit: A calm day has no breeze; a close room lacks ventilation.

clue.text: Witch being one, from which he makes distinction

definitions.text: Witch being one, from which he makes distinction

parts.words: Witch being one, from which he makes distinction
parts.note: a sorceress casts charms, and someone good at orthography tells the homophones witch and which apart

explanation.surface: A sorceress and the person who knows how to tell her apart.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a caster of charms and someone who writes words correctly.

clue.text: Hybrid character gets direction to apply elsewhere

parts.note: a cross is a hybrid of two breeds
a reference is a testimonial to one's character

explanation.surface: A mixed-race person is told to look for work somewhere else.
explanation.definitionFit: A note in a book telling the reader to look at another passage for information.

clue.text: Need about everything

parts.note: C, for circa, means about
all means everything

explanation.surface: Something is required regarding the whole lot.
explanation.definitionFit: As in 'there's no call for it': demand or requirement.

clue.text: Untouchable? Beside the point

definitions.meaning: having no physical body, so not able to be felt

explanation.definitionFit: Something incorporeal cannot be touched; something irrelevant does not matter.

clue.text: Pole, getting two-points, can't be dense

parts.note: a spar is a pole, as on a ship
S, south, is a compass point
E, east, is another compass point

explanation.surface: A pole vaulter scoring two points cannot be stupid.
explanation.definitionFit: Thinly scattered growth or population is the opposite of thick or crowded.

clue.text: To renounce it might make one far worse

indicators.note: might make suggests the letters could be rearranged into a new word

explanation.surface: Giving up something could leave you much worse off.
explanation.definitionFit: To forswear is to give up or abjure solemnly.
